idiom_name: package-scoped domain type: struct + methods + New* constructor
implementation_notes: Go has no classes and no type-level access control, so the pattern's encapsulation is replaced by the package boundary: unexported fields, exported behaviour methods, and NewXxx constructors that validate and return (*X, error). Value objects are small named types with their own constructors (an EmailAddress that validates at parse time), interfaces are declared by the consumer for collaboration seams, and closed value sets are constants with a String method. Inheritance is replaced by embedding and composition, and persistence lives in a different package whose adapter converts domain structs to and from rows - being outside the package it cannot touch the fields.
pitfalls: Same-package code - including a persistence adapter you accidentally place next to the model - can still write the unexported fields; keep mappers in their own package.
The zero value is constructible without the constructor: either make it meaningful (an empty, harmless state) or guard every method against it.
Exporting slices or maps exposes internal state; return copies (slices.Clone) or narrow read-only accessors.
